stages.note: Skip this stage if you already have an AWS identity that can create IAM roles and that is not the root user. A new AWS account has only the root user. Do not use the root user for the PoC: make a separate identity. Choose path A (single sign-on, recommended for teams) or path B (one IAM user with an access key, faster).

steps.who: You, in the AWS console as root
steps.d: Sign in at console.aws.amazon.com as the root user. Open the account menu (your account name, top right) › Security credentials › Multi-factor authentication › Assign MFA device. Follow the steps for an authenticator app or a security key.

steps.h: Path A, step 1: turn on IAM Identity Center
steps.d: In the top search bar, type IAM Identity Center and open it. Select a region at the top right, for example us-east-1 or the region nearest to you. Click Enable, then Enable with AWS Organizations. AWS creates an organization for your account. Write down the region.

steps.h: Path A, step 2: create your user
steps.d: Open Users › Add user. Enter a user name, your email address and your name, then click Next twice and Add user. AWS sends an invitation email: accept it and set a password and MFA.

steps.h: Path A, step 3: give the user administrator rights
steps.d: Open Permission sets › Create permission set › Predefined permission set › AdministratorAccess › Next › Next › Create. Then open AWS accounts, select your account, click Assign users or groups, select your user, then the AdministratorAccess permission set, and Submit.

steps.h: Path A, step 4: copy the access portal URL
steps.d: Open Dashboard. In Settings summary, copy the AWS access portal URL (it looks like https://d-1234567890.awsapps.com/start). Sign out of the root user. From now on, sign in through this URL.

steps.h: Path B, step 1: create an IAM user
steps.d: Open IAM › Users › Create user. User name: poc-admin. Do not give console access. Next › Attach policies directly › select AdministratorAccess › Next › Create user.

steps.h: Path B, step 2: create an access key
steps.d: Open the user poc-admin › Security credentials › Create access key › Command Line Interface (CLI). Confirm the note and click Next › Create access key. Copy the Access key ID and the Secret access key: AWS shows the secret only once. Keep both secret, and delete the key after the PoC (same page › Actions › Deactivate, then Delete). Sign out of the root user.

stages.t: Sign in to AWS from the terminal

steps.h: Sign in to AWS from the terminal
steps.who: You, in a terminal and the browser
steps.d: Use the identity from the stage “Set up your AWS account”. Path A (single sign-on): run aws configure sso --use-device-code (on Windows the browser cannot open from WSL; the command prints a link and a code: open the link in your Windows browser, sign in, enter the code). Answers: SSO session name: any name. SSO start URL: your AWS access portal URL (in the AWS console, IAM Identity Center, dashboard). SSO region: the region where you turned on IAM Identity Center (the region selector at the top right of that console). Registration scopes: press Enter. Then select the account you chose for the PoC (a new dedicated account; an existing account only after the approval in Multicloud connect-aws, Rule 6) and the role with full administrator rights (AdministratorAccess, or another admin role such as SystemAdministrator). Never choose the root login. Default client region: us-east-1. Output format: json (press Enter). Profile name: poc. Path B (access key): run aws configure --profile poc and paste the access key ID and secret access key; region us-east-1; output json.

in.label: Path B: access key ID and secret

os.mac:
aws configure sso          # path A
aws configure --profile poc   # path B
export AWS_PROFILE=poc
aws sts get-caller-identity
os.linux:
aws configure sso          # path A
aws configure --profile poc   # path B
export AWS_PROFILE=poc
aws sts get-caller-identity
os.win:
# In the Ubuntu window
aws configure sso          # path A
aws configure --profile poc   # path B
export AWS_PROFILE=poc
aws sts get-caller-identity

steps.g: The Account value in the output is your 12-digit AWS account ID. You need it in the next stage. Never paste keys into an AI chat. Path A: if your sign-in expires later, run aws sso login --profile poc. No browser opens (Windows with WSL, SSH): press Ctrl+C and run aws configure sso --use-device-code (later: aws sso login --profile poc --use-device-code).
